=== FINDINGS FROM mistralai_mistral-small-2603 ===
- File: scripts/review_apply_fixes.sh
  Code: kill "${wd_pid}" 2>/dev/null || true; wait "${wd_pid}" 2>/dev/null || true
  Problem: The watchdog subshell exits on its own (exit codes 142/143/144) after killing the editor, so the parent's `kill` can hit a process that is already gone and return 1 (ESRCH). Under `set -euo pipefail`, this unguarded failure aborts the entire script, preventing retry attempts, fallback summaries, and stderr archiving.
  Runtime impact: The editor step fails completely instead of moving to the next attempt, causing the run to surface as "editor produced no output — will retry" and deferring to the stall poller, wasting budget and requiring another full reviewer pass.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- File: scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh
  Code: kill "${wd_pid}" 2>/dev/null || true; wait "${wd_pid}" 2>/dev/null || true
  Problem: Same issue as above — the reviewer watchdog subshell exits on its own after killing the reviewer process, so an unguarded `kill` returns 1 under `set -euo pipefail`, aborting the reviewer attempt.
  Runtime impact: Reviewer attempts fail completely instead of moving to the next model or attempt, wasting reviewer budget and delaying progress.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- File: scripts/review_apply_fixes.sh:2054-2065
  Code: kill "${wd_pid}" 2>/dev/null || true; wait "${wd_pid}" 2>/dev/null || true
  Problem: The reap line lacks explicit error handling for the case where the watchdog has already exited, relying solely on `|| true` which masks the underlying issue without documenting why it's safe.
  Runtime impact: None once the fix is applied, but the lack of explicit comment explaining the expected outcome could confuse future maintainers.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
- File: scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh:3960, 4011
  Code: kill "${wd_pid}" 2>/dev/null || true; wait "${wd_pid}" 2>/dev/null || true

=== FINDINGS FROM moonshotai_kimi-k3 ===
- File: tests/test_editor_watchdog_kill_contract.py (entire file); absence in .github/workflows/ci.yml
  Line or code reference: tests/test_editor_watchdog_kill_contract.py:75-101; compare .github/workflows/ci.yml:561-565 ("Review editor stderr-drain unit tests" step, which wires the directly analogous watchdog-adjacent test tests/test_review_editor_fifo_drain.py)
  Problem: The new regression test is not wired into any CI or release-gate workflow, so it never runs outside a local checkout.
  Why it fails at runtime: A repo-wide search for "test_editor_watchdog_kill_contract" matches only changelog.d/4071-editor-watchdog-kill-abort.md:11 — no workflow references it. This repo has no directory-wide pytest invocation: every test file is executed via an explicit per-file step in .github/workflows/ci.yml (and the release gates' "Unit tests" steps in mark-stable.yml:318+ and test-and-mark-stable.yml:3623+), a convention documented in-repo at tests/test_stall_recovery_pr_lookup.py:1103 ("ci.yml runs each test as python3 tests/<file>.py") and enforced by precedent in tests/test_opencode_live_smoke_workflow.py:130 (test_focused_tests_are_wired_into_ci). As shipped, if someone reverts the `|| true` guards on the three watchdog reap lines — the exact regression this PR exists to prevent (run 34397466777) — every CI job stays green and the pinned contract silently does nothing. Fix: add the file to the ci.yml step at line 561 (e.g. `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m pytest -q tests/test_editor_watchdog_kill_contract.py` — the pytest form is required because this file, unlike most siblings, has no `if __name__ == "__main__"` main() runner).
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
